**[APPENDIX A: TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS]{.underline}**

This Appendix A is attached to and incorporated into that certain Data Enrichment Agreement dated November 20, 2023, between Meridian Consumer Group, Inc. and Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. (the \"**Agreement**\"). Capitalized terms used herein and not otherwise defined shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement.

**A.1 Data Transfer Method.** Client Data and Enriched Data shall be transmitted via Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) to designated endpoints maintained by each Party. Each Party shall provide the other Party with its designated SFTP endpoint credentials, including hostname, port, and authentication keys, prior to the first data transfer. Transfer frequency shall be monthly, with each monthly transmission to be completed on or before the fifth (5th) business day of each calendar month. Each Party shall be responsible for maintaining the availability and security of its SFTP endpoints and shall provide at least ten (10) business days\' written notice to the other Party of any changes to its endpoint configuration.

**A.2 Client Data Format.** Vanterra shall provide Client Data in delimited flat file format (.csv), using pipe (\"\|\") delimiters and UTF-8 encoding. Each monthly Client Data file shall include the following fields per individual consumer record:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Field Name**                       **Data Type**           **Description**
  ------------------------------------ ----------------------- -----------------------------------------
  Unique User Identifier               VARCHAR(20)             Vanterra internal user ID

  First Name                           VARCHAR(50)             Consumer first name

  Last Name                            VARCHAR(50)             Consumer last name

  Email Address                        VARCHAR(64)             SHA-256 hashed email address

  Street Address                       VARCHAR(100)            Consumer mailing address --- street

  City                                 VARCHAR(50)             Consumer mailing address --- city

  State                                CHAR(2)                 Consumer mailing address --- state code

  ZIP Code                             VARCHAR(10)             Consumer mailing address --- ZIP/ZIP+4

  Date of Birth                        DATE (YYYY-MM-DD)       Consumer date of birth

  Gender                               CHAR(1)                 Consumer gender (M/F/X/U)

  Health Risk Assessment Category      INT (1-5)               Coded HRA category per Vanterra scoring

  Wellness Program Enrollment Status   CHAR(1)                 Enrollment status (Y/N)

  Employer Group Identifier            VARCHAR(15)             Employer group code
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each record shall represent a single individual consumer. Vanterra shall include a header row in each file and shall provide a companion manifest file listing total record count, file checksum (SHA-256), and transmission timestamp.

**A.3 Enriched Data Format.** Meridian shall return Enriched Data in delimited flat file format (.csv), using pipe (\"\|\") delimiters and UTF-8 encoding. Each monthly Enriched Data file shall include the following fields per matched consumer record:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Field Name**                         **Data Type**           **Description**
  -------------------------------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------------
  Vanterra Unique User Identifier        VARCHAR(20)             For re-linking to Vanterra records

  Match Confidence Score                 DECIMAL(3,2)            Score from 0.00 to 1.00

  Purchase Category Affinity Scores      ARRAY(15)               Scores across 15 retail categories

  Loyalty Program Membership Indicator   CHAR(1)                 Y/N

  Loyalty Program Tier                   VARCHAR(20)             Tier designation (if applicable)

  Average Monthly Spend Estimate         DECIMAL(10,2)           Estimated monthly consumer spend

  Purchase Recency Score                 INT                     Days since last recorded purchase

  Lifestyle Segment Code                 VARCHAR(10)             Meridian proprietary segment code

  Household Composition Indicator        VARCHAR(5)              Coded household composition
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Meridian shall include a header row in each file and shall provide a companion manifest file listing total matched record count, average match confidence score, file checksum (SHA-256), and transmission timestamp.

**A.4 Data Volume.** Estimated monthly Client Data submissions shall comprise approximately five hundred thousand (500,000) to seven hundred thousand (700,000) individual consumer records. Estimated monthly Enriched Data returns shall comprise approximately three hundred fifty thousand (350,000) to five hundred thousand (500,000) matched records, reflecting an estimated match rate of sixty-five percent to seventy-five percent (65%--75%). Actual match rates may vary based on the quality and completeness of Client Data and the coverage of Meridian\'s databases. In the event monthly Client Data volumes exceed seven hundred fifty thousand (750,000) records for three (3) or more consecutive months, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an appropriate adjustment to the Annual Service Fee.

**A.5 Data Retention During Term.** Meridian shall maintain the most recent twenty-four (24) months of Client Data in its active processing environment to support data matching, enrichment, and quality assurance activities. Historical Client Data older than twenty-four (24) months shall be migrated to archival storage maintained by Meridian, but shall remain accessible by Meridian for purposes consistent with Section 3.3 of the Agreement, including statistical analysis, model training, and benchmarking.

**A.6 Post-Termination Retention Specifications.** Following termination or expiration of the Agreement, Meridian shall migrate all retained Client Data from its active processing environment to cold archival storage within sixty (60) days of the effective date of termination or expiration. Archived Client Data shall be retained for the full seven (7) year Retention Period specified in Section 3.3 of the Agreement. During the archival period, access to archived Client Data shall be limited to Meridian\'s data science and analytics teams and shall be used solely for statistical analysis, model validation, benchmarking, and related analytical purposes. Meridian shall apply commercially reasonable de-identification measures to archived Client Data; provided, however, that Meridian shall not be required to delete original identifiers if such identifiers are necessary for the integrity of statistical models, longitudinal analysis, or match validation processes. Upon expiration of the seven (7) year Retention Period, Meridian shall destroy all remaining copies of Client Data in its possession or control and shall provide written certification of such destruction to Vanterra within thirty (30) days.

**[APPENDIX B: DATA CATEGORIES AND PERMITTED USES]{.underline}**

This Appendix B is attached to and incorporated into that certain Data Enrichment Agreement dated November 20, 2023, between Meridian Consumer Group, Inc. and Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. (the \"**Agreement**\"). Capitalized terms used herein and not otherwise defined shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement.

**B.1 Categories of Client Data Provided by Vanterra.**

> **Category 1 --- Identifiers:** Consumer name (first and last), email address (hashed), mailing address (street, city, state, ZIP code), and Vanterra unique user identifier.
>
> **Category 2 --- Demographics:** Date of birth, gender, and employer group identifier.
>
> **Category 3 --- Health & Wellness:** Health risk assessment category (coded 1--5 per Vanterra\'s proprietary scoring methodology) and wellness program enrollment status.

**B.2 Categories of Meridian Data.**

> **Category 1 --- Purchase History:** Transaction records and purchase summaries sourced from Meridian\'s retail partners, e-commerce platforms, and pharmacy chains, including product category information, transaction frequency, and transaction value ranges.
>
> **Category 2 --- Loyalty Program Data:** Loyalty program membership status, tier designation, reward redemption patterns, and program engagement metrics sourced from Meridian\'s loyalty program partners.
>
> **Category 3 --- Consumer Behavioral Segments:** Meridian\'s proprietary lifestyle and spending segments, derived from Meridian\'s analytical models and applied to consumer records based on observed purchase behavior and loyalty program activity.

**B.3 Permitted Uses by Vanterra.** Vanterra may use Enriched Data solely for the following purposes:

> \(a\) enhancement and refinement of Vanterra\'s predictive wellness scoring models;
>
> \(b\) personalization of user experiences within Vanterra\'s digital health platform, including tailored content, recommendations, and program offerings;
>
> \(c\) wellness program design, optimization, and evaluation; and
>
> \(d\) employer reporting and program analytics, provided that any data included in employer-facing reports shall be presented in de-identified, aggregate form only and shall not identify any individual consumer.

**B.4 Permitted Uses by Meridian.** Meridian may use Client Data solely to perform the Enrichment Services described in the Agreement, including data matching, cross-referencing, appending, and scoring activities necessary for the delivery of Enriched Data. Following termination or expiration of the Agreement, Meridian may continue to use retained Client Data in accordance with the post-termination retention and use rights described in Section 3.3 of the Agreement and Section A.6 of Appendix A, including for archival, statistical analysis, benchmarking, and model training and validation purposes.

**B.5 Prohibited Uses.** Neither Party shall use data provided by the other Party under this Agreement for any of the following purposes:

> \(a\) discriminatory profiling or targeting of consumers based on protected class status, including race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, or genetic information;
>
> \(b\) determining eligibility for, or setting the terms of, credit, insurance, employment, housing, or education, or for any purpose that would cause the data to be considered a \"consumer report\" under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq.);
>
> \(c\) any purpose that would violate applicable federal, state, or local law, rule, or regulation; or
>
> \(d\) any purpose not expressly authorized under this Agreement or a mutually executed statement of work.

*\[End of Appendix B\]*

*\[End of Agreement\]*

**[JOINT ANALYTICS COLLABORATION AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Agreement Number: CPB-VHS-2022-0601**

by and between

**VANTERRA HEALTH SOLUTIONS, INC.** a Delaware corporation (\"Vanterra\" or \"Company\")

and

**CLEARPOINT BEHAVIORAL, LLC** an Illinois limited liability company (\"ClearPoint\" or \"Analytics Partner\")

**Effective Date: June 1, 2022**

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. is a digital health platform offering employer-sponsored wellness programs, biometric screenings, and health risk assessments to consumers throughout the United States, with its principal offices located at 4200 Torrey Pines Road, Suite 310, San Diego, California 92130;

**WHEREAS**, ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC is a provider of cross-device identity resolution and online behavioral analytics services, with its principal offices located at 200 North Michigan Avenue, Suite 1450, Chicago, Illinois 60601;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to enter into a joint analytics collaboration to enhance each Party\'s understanding of consumer behavior across digital touchpoints through the mutual exchange of complementary datasets and the generation of enriched behavioral profiles;

**WHEREAS**, Vanterra possesses valuable user-level data including hashed email addresses, device identifiers, in-app behavioral data, and related account information collected in the course of operating its digital health platform, and ClearPoint possesses cross-device identity graph data and enriched browsing behavioral profiles compiled from a broad network of online sources;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties believe that the reciprocal exchange of data and collaborative analytics will generate mutual value, improved consumer experiences, and enhanced business intelligence for both Parties; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties wish to set forth the terms and conditions governing their respective rights and obligations in connection with such joint analytics collaboration;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual promises, covenants, and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the context in which they appear.

**1.1 \"Agreement\"** means this Joint Analytics Collaboration Agreement, including all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto, as may be amended from time to time in accordance with Section 12.4.

**1.2 \"Analytics Outputs\"** means the enriched data profiles, insights, reports, analytical models, statistical summaries, and derived datasets generated through the Collaboration Activities.

**1.3 \"Collaboration Activities\"** means the mutual exchange of Contributed Data between the Parties, the matching and linking of consumer records across platforms and devices, the creation of enriched behavioral profiles from combined data sources, and the generation of Analytics Outputs, in each case as described in Article 2 and Article 3 of this Agreement.

**1.4 \"Contributed Data\"** means the data elements provided by each Party to the other Party pursuant to Article 3 and Exhibit A hereto.

**1.5 \"ClearPoint Data\"** means the cross-device identity graph data, browsing behavior data, interest segment classifications, behavioral propensity scores, and enriched behavioral profiles owned or controlled by ClearPoint and contributed to the Collaboration Activities pursuant to this Agreement.

**1.6 \"Enriched Profiles\"** means the combined consumer behavioral profiles generated by ClearPoint through the matching and linking of Vanterra Data with ClearPoint Data and other third-party data sources maintained by ClearPoint, including cross-device behavioral attributes, interest segment classifications, and propensity scores.

**1.7 \"Fees\"** means the annual collaboration fees and any other amounts payable by Vanterra to ClearPoint as set forth in Article 5 of this Agreement.

**1.8 \"Party\"** means Vanterra or ClearPoint individually, and **\"Parties\"** means Vanterra and ClearPoint collectively.

**1.9 \"Personal Information\"** has the meaning given to such term under the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq.).

**1.10 \"Term\"** has the meaning set forth in Article 8 of this Agreement.

**1.11 \"Transfer Protocol\"** means the data transfer method specified in Article 4 and Exhibit B hereto.

**1.12 \"Vanterra Data\"** means the user-level data elements owned or controlled by Vanterra and contributed to the Collaboration Activities pursuant to this Agreement, as specified in Article 3 and Exhibit A, including but not limited to hashed email addresses, mobile device identifiers, app usage data, device IDs, and related user account information.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF COLLABORATION]{.underline}**

**2.1 Purpose.** The purpose of this Agreement is to establish a comprehensive framework for a joint analytics collaboration whereby each Party contributes complementary datasets to enable cross-device identity resolution, behavioral analytics, and the creation of Enriched Profiles for each Party\'s respective business purposes. The Parties intend that the Collaboration Activities will yield data-driven insights that improve each Party\'s ability to understand and serve consumers across digital touchpoints.

**2.2 Scope.** The Collaboration Activities encompassed by this Agreement include the following:

> \(a\) the exchange of Contributed Data between the Parties in accordance with the specifications, formats, and schedules set forth in Article 3 and Exhibit A;
>
> \(b\) ClearPoint\'s matching and linking of Vanterra user records across devices using ClearPoint\'s proprietary identity resolution technology and cross-device identity graph;
>
> \(c\) ClearPoint\'s generation of Enriched Profiles incorporating cross-device behavioral data, browsing history categorizations, interest segment classifications, and behavioral propensity scores derived from the combined datasets;
>
> \(d\) the return delivery of Enriched Profiles to Vanterra for use in in-app content recommendations, user engagement optimization, and personalization of wellness program communications; and
>
> \(e\) ClearPoint\'s use of Vanterra Data to enhance, update, and expand its own identity graph, behavioral analytics capabilities, and related data assets in the ordinary course of ClearPoint\'s business.

**2.3 Mutual Benefit.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Collaboration Activities are designed to provide mutual value to both Parties. Vanterra receives Enriched Profiles and cross-device linking capabilities that enable more effective personalization of its digital health platform offerings. ClearPoint receives Vanterra Data, which strengthens and expands ClearPoint\'s identity resolution products, behavioral data offerings, and overall data graph coverage. Each Party enters into this Agreement with the understanding that the collaboration yields significant and reciprocal business benefits to both Parties.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- DATA EXCHANGE AND CONTRIBUTED DATA]{.underline}**

**3.1 Vanterra Contributed Data.** Vanterra shall provide ClearPoint with the data elements specified below and further detailed in Exhibit A, on a weekly basis, in accordance with the Transfer Protocol and schedule set forth in Article 4 and Exhibit B:

> \(a\) Hashed email addresses associated with Vanterra user accounts;
>
> \(b\) Full user names associated with Vanterra account records;
>
> \(c\) Mobile device identifiers, including Apple Identifier for Advertisers (IDFA) and Google Advertising Identifier (GAID);
>
> \(d\) Device IDs, including browser cookie identifiers and device fingerprints;
>
> \(e\) App session data, including session start and end timestamps and duration metrics; and
>
> \(f\) In-app feature interaction data, including features accessed, content viewed, and actions taken within the Vanterra platform.

The specific data types, formats, and field-level specifications for each Vanterra Contributed Data element are set forth in Table A-1 of Exhibit A. Vanterra shall ensure that all data files conform to the format requirements described in Exhibit A and Exhibit B.

**3.2 ClearPoint Contributed Data.** ClearPoint shall provide Vanterra with the following data elements, as further described in Table A-2 of Exhibit A:

> \(a\) Enriched Profiles matched to Vanterra user records, including cross-device behavioral data, browsing history categories, and interest segment classifications;
>
> \(b\) Cross-device linkage maps connecting Vanterra device IDs across ClearPoint\'s proprietary device graph, enabling Vanterra to understand multi-device user journeys; and
>
> \(c\) Behavioral propensity scores derived from online browsing patterns and interest-based models, segmented according to ClearPoint\'s proprietary audience taxonomy.

ClearPoint shall deliver the foregoing data elements to Vanterra in accordance with the delivery schedule and file formats specified in Exhibit A and Exhibit B.

**3.3 Data Matching.** ClearPoint shall use commercially reasonable efforts to match Vanterra Contributed Data against ClearPoint\'s existing identity graph to create Enriched Profiles. ClearPoint may combine Vanterra Data with data from ClearPoint\'s other data sources, partners, and third-party data providers to improve matching accuracy, expand device graph coverage, and enhance profile completeness. ClearPoint shall use its proprietary deterministic and probabilistic matching algorithms to link Vanterra user records to known device identifiers and behavioral profiles within ClearPoint\'s systems.

**3.4 Data Quality.** Each Party represents and warrants that its Contributed Data is accurate and current to the best of its knowledge as of the date of transmission. Neither Party guarantees one hundred percent (100%) match rates, data completeness, or the absence of errors, duplicates, or stale records. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain the quality and currency of its Contributed Data throughout the Term.

**3.5 Use of Vanterra Data by ClearPoint.** Except as expressly set forth in this Agreement, ClearPoint may use Vanterra Data contributed pursuant to this Article 3 to enhance, update, supplement, and improve its identity resolution graph, behavioral analytics products, audience segmentation capabilities, and related data offerings. ClearPoint shall have the right to process, analyze, aggregate, and derive insights from Vanterra Data in connection with ClearPoint\'s general business operations, subject to the confidentiality obligations set forth in Article 9.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- DATA TRANSFER SPECIFICATIONS]{.underline}**

**4.1 Transfer Protocol.** All data transfers between the Parties shall be conducted via File Transfer Protocol (FTP) in accordance with the technical specifications set forth in Exhibit B. Each Party shall maintain an FTP server environment capable of receiving data files from the other Party in the manner described in Exhibit B.

**4.2 Transfer Schedule.** Vanterra shall upload Contributed Data files to ClearPoint\'s designated FTP server no less frequently than once per calendar week. ClearPoint shall process received Vanterra Data files and return Enriched Profiles and other ClearPoint Contributed Data to Vanterra\'s designated FTP server within five (5) business days of receipt of each Vanterra Contributed Data file. Data uploads shall occur during the transfer window specified in Exhibit B unless the Parties mutually agree to an alternative schedule.

**4.3 File Format.** Vanterra Contributed Data files shall be transmitted in comma-separated value (.csv) format. ClearPoint Contributed Data files shall be transmitted in JavaScript Object Notation (.json) format. Field-level specifications, delimiters, encoding, and naming conventions are set forth in Exhibit B.

**4.4 FTP Credentials.** Each Party shall provide the other Party with the necessary FTP server address, port number, username, and password credentials required to access its designated FTP server. FTP credentials shall be communicated via electronic mail to the designated technical contacts of each Party. Credentials shall be updated and rotated no less frequently than once per calendar year.

**4.5 Data Integrity.** Each Party shall include a record count and a checksum hash (MD5 or SHA-256) with each transmitted data file for purposes of integrity verification. The receiving Party shall validate the record count and checksum upon receipt and shall notify the sending Party within twenty-four (24) hours if a discrepancy is detected. In the event of a discrepancy, the sending Party shall re-transmit the affected file within twenty-four (24) hours of notification.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**5.1 Annual Collaboration Fee.** In consideration of ClearPoint\'s identity resolution services, Enriched Profile generation, and participation in the Collaboration Activities, Vanterra shall pay ClearPoint an annual collaboration fee of Nine Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$950,000.00) (the \"Annual Fee\") during each year of the Term.

**5.2 Payment Terms.** The Annual Fee shall be payable in equal quarterly installments of Two Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$237,500.00) each. Quarterly installments shall be due and payable on the first business day of each calendar quarter during the Term (i.e., October 1, January 1, April 1, and July 1). All payments shall be made by wire transfer or ACH payment to the bank account designated by ClearPoint in writing. Late payments shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less.

**5.3 Fee Adjustments.** ClearPoint may increase the Annual Fee by no more than five percent (5%) per annum upon written notice to Vanterra at least sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of any renewal Term. Any such fee increase shall take effect at the beginning of the applicable renewal Term and shall remain in effect for the duration of that renewal period unless further adjusted in accordance with this Section.

**5.4 Expenses.** Each Party shall bear its own costs and expenses incurred in connection with the performance of Collaboration Activities, including without limitation data processing costs, storage and infrastructure expenses, personnel costs, and technology maintenance expenditures. Neither Party shall be entitled to reimbursement from the other Party for any such expenses unless otherwise agreed in writing.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DATA OWNERSHIP]{.underline}**

**6.1 Ownership of Contributed Data.** Each Party retains all right, title, and interest in and to its respective Contributed Data, including all intellectual property rights therein. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer ownership of either Party\'s pre-existing data assets, proprietary technology, or intellectual property to the other Party, except as expressly provided in this Article 6.

**6.2 Ownership of Analytics Outputs.** Analytics Outputs and Enriched Profiles generated by ClearPoint through the Collaboration Activities shall be jointly owned by the Parties. Each Party shall have the unrestricted right to use, reproduce, license, distribute, sublicense, and commercialize Analytics Outputs independently and without accounting to, or obtaining the consent of, the other Party. Neither Party shall have any obligation to share revenues, profits, or other proceeds derived from its independent use or commercialization of Analytics Outputs.

**6.3 ClearPoint\'s Identity Graph.** Vanterra acknowledges and agrees that ClearPoint may incorporate data linkages, device associations, cross-device mapping relationships, and behavioral insights derived from or informed by Vanterra Data into ClearPoint\'s proprietary identity graph and data products. Once incorporated, such data linkages, associations, and derived insights shall become part of ClearPoint\'s proprietary data assets and may be used, licensed, and commercialized by ClearPoint in the ordinary course of its business without restriction.

**6.4 No License Back.** Except as expressly provided in this Agreement, neither Party grants to the other Party any license, right, or interest in or to its intellectual property, trademarks, trade names, service marks, patents, copyrights, trade secrets, or proprietary technology. Each Party\'s use of the other Party\'s Contributed Data shall be limited to the purposes expressly contemplated by this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- PRIVACY AND DATA PROTECTION]{.underline}**

**7.1 Compliance with Applicable Law.** Each Party shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations governing the collection, use, storage, processing, and disclosure of personal information, including without limitation the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 (\"CCPA\") (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq.) and any regulations promulgated thereunder. Each Party shall be solely responsible for ensuring that its own data collection practices, privacy policies, and consumer-facing disclosures comply with applicable law.

**7.2 No Sale or Sharing.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that the exchange of Contributed Data under this Agreement does not constitute a \"sale\" of personal information as defined under the CCPA. The Parties characterize the data exchange contemplated herein as a joint analytics collaboration for mutual business benefit, in which each Party contributes complementary datasets to enable the generation of Analytics Outputs and Enriched Profiles. Each Party shall maintain internal records and documentation consistent with this characterization.

**7.3 Consumer Requests.** In the event that either Party receives a verifiable consumer request for access to, deletion of, or opt-out relating to Contributed Data or Analytics Outputs that includes or was derived from the other Party\'s data, the receiving Party shall promptly notify the other Party of such request, and in no event later than ten (10) business days following receipt. Each Party shall be independently responsible for responding to consumer requests directed to it in accordance with its own privacy policies and applicable law. Nothing in this Section 7.3 shall be construed as requiring either Party to modify, delete, or cease processing data on behalf of the other Party unless expressly required by applicable law.

**7.4 Representations Regarding Consent.** Each Party represents and warrants that it has obtained all necessary consents, authorizations, and permissions from consumers, as required under applicable law, for the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information contributed under this Agreement. Each Party shall maintain documentation of such consents and authorizations and shall make such documentation available to the other Party upon reasonable request.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**8.1 Initial Term.** This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect through September 30, 2025 (the \"Initial Term\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 8.

**8.2 Renewal.** Following the expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of one (1) year each (each, a \"Renewal Term\"), commencing on October 1, 2025 and on each anniversary thereof, unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least ninety (90) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term. The Initial Term together with any Renewal Terms shall be referred to collectively as the \"Term.\"

**8.3 Termination for Cause.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within such thirty (30)-day notice period. For the avoidance of doubt, a failure to cure within the notice period shall entitle the non-breaching Party to terminate this Agreement immediately upon expiration of such period.

**8.4 Termination for Convenience.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement at any time, without cause, upon one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party. In the event of termination for convenience by Vanterra, Vanterra shall remain obligated to pay all Fees accrued through the effective date of termination, including any pro-rated quarterly installment for the quarter in which termination becomes effective.

**8.5 Effect of Termination.** Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason:

> \(a\) Each Party shall cease all use of the other Party\'s Contributed Data within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination, except as otherwise permitted under this Section 8.5;
>
> \(b\) Analytics Outputs jointly owned under Section 6.2 may continue to be used by each Party after termination, subject to the confidentiality obligations set forth in Article 9;
>
> \(c\) ClearPoint may retain data linkages, device associations, and derived insights that have been incorporated into ClearPoint\'s proprietary identity graph pursuant to Section 6.3; and
>
> \(d\) All payment obligations accrued prior to the effective date of termination shall survive and remain enforceable.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**9.1 Confidential Information.** Each Party acknowledges that, in the course of performing its obligations under this Agreement, it may receive or have access to confidential and proprietary information of the other Party. The Contributed Data, Analytics Outputs, the terms and conditions of this Agreement, all financial information exchanged between the Parties, and each Party\'s proprietary technology, trade secrets, and business strategies shall constitute \"Confidential Information\" of the disclosing Party.

**9.2 Non-Disclosure.** Neither Party shall disclose, publish, or disseminate the other Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing Party, except: (a) as required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process (provided that the receiving Party shall provide the disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement to the extent permitted by law); (b) as necessary to perform its obligations under this Agreement, to employees, contractors, and advisors who have a need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth herein; or (c) as otherwise expressly permitted under this Agreement.

**9.3 Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding Section 9.2, ClearPoint may disclose, distribute, license, or otherwise make available Analytics Outputs to its clients, customers, and business partners in the ordinary course of its data analytics business, provided that such disclosures are consistent with ClearPoint\'s standard data licensing practices and do not include the disclosure of Vanterra\'s Confidential Information other than as incorporated into Analytics Outputs.

**9.4 Survival.** The obligations of the Parties under this Article 9 shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of such termination or expiration.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**

**10.1 Mutual Representations.** Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that:

> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of formation;
>
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
>
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action and do not conflict with, or result in a breach of, any other agreement, obligation, or instrument to which such Party is bound; and
>
> \(d\) it shall perform its obligations under this Agreement in a professional, diligent, and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards and practices.

**10.2 ClearPoint Representations.** ClearPoint represents and warrants that its identity resolution technology, behavioral data products, and analytics methodologies are developed and maintained in compliance with applicable industry standards and all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. ClearPoint further represents that the ClearPoint Data provided hereunder does not infringe upon the intellectual property rights or proprietary rights of any third party.

**10.3 Vanterra Representations.** Vanterra represents and warrants that it has the right and authority to contribute Vanterra Data for the purposes described herein, and that such contribution does not infringe on any third-party rights, violate any contractual obligations to which Vanterra is bound, or violate any applicable federal, state, or local laws or regulations.

**10.4 Disclaimer of Warranties.** EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATIONS OR WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, OR RELIABILITY OF DATA. ALL CONTRIBUTED DATA, ANALYTICS OUTPUTS, AND ENRICHED PROFILES ARE PROVIDED ON AN \"AS IS\" AND \"AS AVAILABLE\" BASIS.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY AND INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**11.1 Limitation of Liability.** EXCEPT FOR BREACHES OF ARTICLE 9 (CONFIDENTIALITY) OR A PARTY\'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTIONS 11.2 AND 11.3, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY\'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF FEES ACTUALLY PAID OR PAYABLE BY VANTERRA TO CLEARPOINT DURING THE TWELVE (12)-MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE DATE ON WHICH THE CLAIM FIRST AROSE.

**11.2 Indemnification by ClearPoint.** ClearPoint shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Vanterra, its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against any and all third-party claims, demands, actions, suits, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising out of or relating to: (a) ClearPoint\'s material breach of any representation, warranty, or obligation under this Agreement; or (b) ClearPoint\'s violation of any applicable law, rule, or regulation in connection with its processing, use, or disclosure of Contributed Data or Analytics Outputs.

**11.3 Indemnification by Vanterra.** Vanterra shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless ClearPoint, its members, managers, officers, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from and against any and all third-party claims, demands, actions, suits, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising out of or relating to: (a) Vanterra\'s material breach of any representation, warranty, or obligation under this Agreement; (b) Vanterra\'s violation of any applicable law, rule, or regulation in connection with its collection, contribution, or processing of Vanterra Data; or (c) any claim that the Vanterra Data or Vanterra\'s contribution thereof infringes upon or misappropriates the intellectual property rights or proprietary rights of any third party.

**11.4 Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION DAMAGES FOR LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, LOSS OF DATA, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, REGARDLESS OF THE FORM OF ACTION OR THE THEORY OF LIABILITY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**12.1 Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-law rules or principles that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**12.2 Dispute Resolution.** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association in accordance with its then-current Commercial Arbitration Rules. The arbitration shall take place in Chicago, Illinois. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator mutually agreed upon by the Parties, or in the absence of agreement, appointed in accordance with the applicable rules. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final, binding, and enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction. Each Party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees in connection with any arbitration, unless the arbitrator determines otherwise.

**12.3 Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, including all Exhibits and Schedules attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, between the Parties relating to such subject matter.

**12.4 Amendment.** This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

**12.5 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign, delegate, or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided, however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party\'s consent in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of such Party\'s assets, so long as the assignee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement.

**12.6 Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that, to the extent possible, achieves the original intent and economic effect of the invalid provision.

**12.7 Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given: (a) upon personal delivery; (b) one (1) business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service, prepaid, with tracking confirmation; (c) three (3) business days after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or (d) upon confirmed receipt if sent by electronic mail with a copy sent by one of the foregoing methods. All notices shall be addressed to the Parties at the addresses set forth on the signature page hereof, or to such other address as a Party may designate by written notice to the other Party.

**12.8 Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable to the other Party for any failure or delay in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement (other than payment obligations) to the extent that such failure or delay results from any cause beyond such Party\'s reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, natural disasters, epidemics, pandemics, war, terrorism, civil unrest, strikes, labor disputes, government actions or orders, interruptions of power or telecommunications services, cyberattacks, or failures of third-party service providers. **Data Element Notes**

1\. **Email Address Hashing**: Vanterra shall apply the SHA-256 hashing algorithm to all email addresses prior to inclusion in data transmission files. ClearPoint shall maintain a corresponding SHA-256 hashed email index to facilitate deterministic matching.

2\. **Full Name**: Full name data is transmitted in plain-text format to facilitate ClearPoint\'s probabilistic matching algorithms where deterministic matching based on hashed email is unsuccessful. Full names are used for matching purposes only and are not incorporated into ClearPoint\'s externally facing data products.

3\. **Mobile Device IDs**: IDFA and GAID values are transmitted in their raw format to enable direct lookup within ClearPoint\'s device graph. Vanterra shall transmit null values for users who have opted out of ad tracking at the operating system level.

4\. **Enriched Profiles**: ClearPoint\'s Enriched Behavioral Profiles include data derived from ClearPoint\'s proprietary network of publisher and data partners. Records shall be keyed by NTCID as the primary identifier. Secondary match fields available for Vanterra\'s data matching purposes include ADDRESS_HASH (SHA-256 hash of standardized postal address) and ZIP5/ZIP4 combination.

NexTier maintains a suppression file of consumers who have submitted opt-out requests directly to NexTier requesting exclusion from public data compilations. Each delivery shall be accompanied by a manifest file (plain text format) containing: (a) total record count; (b) record count by record status (Active, Updated, Suppress); (c) MD5 checksum for file integrity verification; and (d) delivery timestamp in UTC.

**[CONFIDENTIAL]{.underline}**

**[Internal Privacy Audit Report]{.underline}**

**Assessment of Data Broker Relationships and CPRA Compliance**

 

**Prepared for:** Claire Matsuda Vice President of Legal & Chief Privacy Officer Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. 4200 Torrey Pines Road, Suite 310 San Diego, CA 92130

 

**Prepared by:** Pinehurst Compliance Advisors Privacy & Data Governance Practice

 

**Date:** May 30, 2025

**Engagement Reference:** PCA-2025-VHS-0417

 

ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- This report was prepared at the direction of Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc.\'s legal department and is protected by attorney-client privilege and work product doctrine. This report contains confidential and privileged information intended solely for the use of the designated recipients. Do not copy, distribute, or disclose this report or any of its contents without prior written approval from the Vice President of Legal & Chief Privacy Officer.

**[1. Executive Summary]{.underline}**

Pinehurst Compliance Advisors (\"Pinehurst\") was engaged by the legal department of Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. (\"Vanterra\") under the direction of Claire Matsuda, Vice President of Legal & Chief Privacy Officer, to conduct a comprehensive internal privacy audit assessing Vanterra\'s compliance with the California Privacy Rights Act (\"CPRA\"), as amended, and the California Privacy Protection Agency\'s (\"CPPA\") final regulations (effective March 29, 2024; enforcement commencing July 1, 2024), with specific focus on Vanterra\'s relationships with five third-party data brokers.

The audit was conducted over the period of March 2025 through May 2025. This report was finalized on May 30, 2025. The audit was performed in coordination with Holworth & Kessler LLP, Vanterra\'s outside privacy counsel, to ensure all findings and work product are protected under the attorney-client privilege and work product doctrine.

**Scope.** The audit encompassed a review of all five data broker agreements maintained by Vanterra: DataLume Analytics, LLC; Prismara Insights Corp.; NexTier Data Solutions, Inc.; ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC; and Meridian Consumer Group, Inc. In addition, Pinehurst reviewed Vanterra\'s data processing inventory, consumer-facing privacy disclosures, opt-out and opt-in mechanisms, data transfer infrastructure and protocols, and consumer complaint records for the first half of 2025. The total annual data broker spend across the five relationships is \$3,645,000. Vanterra\'s California user base comprises approximately 620,000 registered users, representing 16.3% of its total 3,800,000 registered users across 42 states.

**Summary of Findings.** Pinehurst identified **17 findings** across **6 critical risk categories**. The findings of greatest severity include:

1\. **Systemic failure to propagate opt-out requests to data brokers.** Consumer opt-out requests are processed only within Vanterra\'s internal systems and are not forwarded to any of the five data brokers. Fourteen consumer complaints specifically requesting deletion from marketing partners were closed without any broker notification.

2\. **Transmission of unencrypted personal information via unsecured FTP.** Plain-text email addresses and full names are transmitted to DataLume Analytics, LLC and ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC via unsecured File Transfer Protocol (FTP) without TLS/SSL encryption.

3\. **Sharing of sensitive personal information without opt-in consent.** Biometric data --- including BMI, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels --- collected through employer-sponsored wellness screenings is transmitted to DataLume for audience segment creation without explicit consumer opt-in consent. No mechanism exists for consumers to limit the use of their sensitive personal information.

4\. **Absence of CPRA-mandated homepage links.** Vanterra\'s website and mobile application do not include a \"Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information\" link or a \"Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information\" link, both of which are required under CPRA.

5\. **Data flows involving approximately 31,000 California minor users without age-gating or affirmative opt-in consent.** Minor user data is not segregated from adult data in any data broker feed, and no affirmative opt-in consent mechanism exists for the sale or sharing of minors\' personal information. Theoretical maximum penalty exposure for this finding alone is \$1,162,500,000.

6\. **Outdated privacy policy lacking CPRA-required disclosures.** Vanterra\'s privacy policy was last updated in April 2023 and does not reflect the enhanced disclosure requirements of the CPPA\'s final regulations.

**Overall Risk Rating: Critical --- Immediate Remediation Required.**

Pinehurst further notes that the CPPA issued an enforcement advisory on January 15, 2025, signaling prioritized enforcement against companies sharing data with unregistered data brokers and failing to honor opt-out requests. Subsequent to the completion of this audit\'s fieldwork, Vanterra received a CPPA inquiry letter dated June 20, 2025, requesting documentation related to data broker relationships, opt-out processing, and data broker registration verification. The response deadline for that inquiry is August 1, 2025, making the findings of this audit immediately relevant and time-sensitive.

**[2. Scope and Methodology]{.underline}**

**2.1 Engagement Overview**

Pinehurst Compliance Advisors was retained in February 2025 by Claire Matsuda, Vice President of Legal & Chief Privacy Officer of Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc., to conduct an internal privacy audit focused on CPRA compliance within Vanterra\'s data broker ecosystem. The engagement was initiated following internal concerns regarding the adequacy of Vanterra\'s privacy infrastructure in light of the CPPA\'s enhanced enforcement posture and the final CPRA implementing regulations that became effective on March 29, 2024.

The audit was conducted in coordination with Holworth & Kessler LLP, Vanterra\'s outside privacy counsel based in San Francisco, to ensure that all audit findings, analyses, and work product are protected under the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. All communications between Pinehurst and the Vanterra legal department regarding this engagement were conducted through or at the direction of counsel. Graymoor Accounting Group, Vanterra\'s external auditor, provided financial data relating to data broker expenditures for the purpose of verification and reconciliation against contractual terms.

**2.2 Audit Scope**

The audit encompassed a review of five data broker agreements currently maintained by Vanterra, each representing a distinct commercial relationship involving the exchange or acquisition of consumer personal information:

1\. **DataLume Analytics, LLC** --- Data Services Agreement, executed January 15, 2023, with an annual contract value of \$1,200,000. DataLume is headquartered in Austin, Texas and provides audience segmentation and behavioral targeting services.

2\. **Prismara Insights Corp.** --- Service Agreement, executed March 1, 2022, with an annual contract value of \$680,000. Prismara is headquartered in New York, New York and provides geolocation and foot-traffic analytics.

3\. **NexTier Data Solutions, Inc.** --- Data License Agreement, executed September 10, 2023, with an annual contract value of \$440,000. NexTier is headquartered in Denver, Colorado and provides demographic and psychographic consumer data.

4\. **ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC** --- Joint Analytics Agreement, executed June 1, 2022, with an annual contract value of \$950,000. ClearPoint is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois and provides cross-device identity resolution and behavioral data enrichment.

5\. **Meridian Consumer Group, Inc.** --- Data Enrichment Agreement, executed November 20, 2023, with an annual contract value of \$375,000. Meridian is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and provides purchase history and loyalty data matching.

The total annual expenditure across all five data broker relationships is \$3,645,000.

The audit assessed the following areas across each of these relationships:

> \(a\) Contractual CPRA compliance provisions, including whether agreements contain updated provisions reflecting CPRA requirements and the CPPA\'s final regulations;
>
> \(b\) Data flow mapping and classification, including the types and categories of personal information exchanged, the direction of data flows, and the methods of transfer;
>
> \(c\) Consumer rights mechanisms, including opt-out of sale/sharing, deletion request processing, and limitation of sensitive personal information;
>
> \(d\) Privacy policy disclosures, including the adequacy of consumer-facing notices regarding data broker relationships;
>
> \(e\) Data transfer security practices, including encryption, authentication, and data minimization;
>
> \(f\) Data broker registration status under California law;
>
> \(g\) Minor user data handling, including age-gating, age verification, and affirmative opt-in consent mechanisms; and
>
> \(h\) Consumer complaint processing, including the completeness of Vanterra\'s response to consumer requests implicating data broker-held data.

In addition to the five data broker agreements, Pinehurst reviewed the following materials:

> • Vanterra\'s data processing inventory, cataloguing 47 distinct data elements across 12 categories;
>
> • Vanterra\'s current consumer-facing privacy policy (last updated April 2023);
>
> • Consumer complaint logs for the period January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2025;
>
> • Technical architecture documentation for data transfer systems, including FTP/SFTP configurations, API specifications, and encryption standards;
>
> • Cookie consent management platform configuration and deployment records;
>
> • The CPPA enforcement advisory dated January 15, 2025; and
>
> • Internal correspondence and operational memoranda provided by the Vanterra privacy team.

**2.3 Methodology.** The audit was conducted in five phases over the period of March through May 2025:

**Phase 1: Document Collection and Review (March 2025).** Pinehurst collected and reviewed all five data broker agreements, including all schedules, amendments, and associated data processing addenda. Pinehurst also obtained Vanterra\'s data processing inventory, privacy policy, consumer complaint logs, and technical architecture documentation. Financial data on data broker spend was obtained from and verified by Graymoor Accounting Group.

**Phase 2: Technical Assessment (March--April 2025).** Pinehurst conducted a technical assessment of Vanterra\'s data transfer infrastructure, including an evaluation of transfer protocols (FTP, SFTP, API), encryption configurations, authentication mechanisms, and data format specifications for each of the five data broker relationships. Packet capture analysis was performed on representative data transfers to verify encryption status and data content.

**Phase 3: Interviews (April 2025).** Pinehurst conducted structured interviews with key Vanterra personnel, including members of the privacy team, engineering leads responsible for data pipeline management, marketing operations staff who manage data broker relationships, and compliance personnel responsible for consumer rights request processing. A total of 12 interviews were conducted across these functional areas.

**Phase 4: Regulatory Gap Analysis (April--May 2025).** Pinehurst conducted a gap analysis comparing Vanterra\'s current practices against the requirements of the CPRA statute (Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100) and the CPPA\'s final implementing regulations (effective March 29, 2024). This analysis identified areas of non-compliance and assigned risk ratings to each finding.

**Phase 5: Report Drafting and Review (May 2025).** Pinehurst prepared this report summarizing all audit findings, risk assessments, and remediation recommendations. The report was reviewed by Pinehurst\'s internal quality assurance team and shared with Holworth & Kessler LLP for privilege review before delivery to Vanterra.

Risk ratings used throughout this report are defined as follows:

> • **Critical**: Immediate regulatory enforcement risk; potential for significant financial penalties; requires remediation within 30 days.
>
> • **High**: Significant compliance gap; likely to attract regulatory attention; requires remediation within 90 days.
>
> • **Medium**: Moderate compliance gap; should be addressed in the normal course of business; remediation within 180 days.
>
> • **Low**: Minor deficiency; best practice improvement recommended; remediation within 12 months.

**2.4 Limitations.** This audit relied on documentation, data, and representations provided by Vanterra personnel. While Pinehurst took reasonable steps to verify the accuracy and completeness of information received, Pinehurst did not independently audit the internal data practices of the five data brokers and cannot confirm the accuracy of representations made by those entities regarding their own data handling. This report does not constitute legal advice. Legal conclusions, including the interpretation of CPRA statutory provisions and the CPPA\'s final regulations, should be confirmed by Holworth & Kessler LLP. Finally, this audit was completed before Vanterra\'s receipt of the CPPA inquiry letter dated June 20, 2025. The findings of this report should be considered in light of that subsequent development and the August 1, 2025 response deadline.

**[3. Company Background and Data Ecosystem Overview]{.underline}**

**3.1 Company Profile**

Vanterra Health Solutions, Inc. is a digital health platform offering employer-sponsored wellness programs, biometric screenings, and health risk assessments. Vanterra\'s platform enables employers to provide comprehensive wellness benefits to their employees and their employees\' dependents, including biometric screening programs, health risk assessment questionnaires, and personalized wellness content.

Vanterra is incorporated in the State of Delaware and maintains its principal offices at 4200 Torrey Pines Road, Suite 310, San Diego, California 92130. The company is publicly traded on the NASDAQ Stock Market under the ticker symbol VHSI. Vanterra employs approximately 1,200 individuals across its corporate headquarters, regional offices, and remote workforce. As of the close of fiscal year 2024, Vanterra reported annual revenue of \$287,000,000 and maintained a registered user base of 3,800,000 individuals across 42 states.

**3.2 California User Population**

Vanterra has approximately 620,000 California-resident registered users, constituting 16.3% of its total user base (620,000 out of 3,800,000 total registered users). This California user population represents a significant and material portion of Vanterra\'s overall business. Of the 620,000 California users, approximately 31,000 are under the age of 16, representing 5.0% of the California user base (31,000 out of 620,000). These minor users primarily access the platform through employer family wellness plans that extend coverage to employees\' dependents, including minor children.

Vanterra clearly meets the threshold requirements for CPRA applicability based on multiple criteria: its annual gross revenue of \$287,000,000 exceeds the \$25,000,000 statutory threshold, and its California user count of 620,000 far exceeds the 100,000-consumer threshold established by the statute.

**3.3 Data Collection Practices**

Vanterra collects extensive personal information from its registered users in connection with the delivery of its digital health and wellness platform services. The nature of Vanterra\'s business --- which involves biometric screenings, health risk assessments, and personalized wellness programming --- necessitates the collection of highly sensitive categories of personal information that extend well beyond what is typical for consumer-facing technology platforms.

Vanterra\'s data processing inventory, which Pinehurst reviewed in its entirety, catalogues 47 distinct data elements across 12 categories. The 12 categories are: (1) Identity Data, (2) Contact Data, (3) Biometric/Health Data, (4) Geolocation Data, (5) Browsing/Behavioral Data, (6) Device/Technical Data, (7) Demographic Data, (8) Employment/Benefits Data, (9) Financial/Insurance Data, (10) Communication Data, (11) Inferred/Derived Data, and (12) User-Generated Content. A complete listing of all 47 data elements organized by category is provided in Appendix A to this report.

Of particular concern to this audit are the following data categories:

**Biometric/Health Data.** Vanterra\'s employer-sponsored wellness screening programs collect biometric data including body mass index (BMI), blood pressure readings, and cholesterol levels. Additionally, health risk assessment questionnaires generate detailed self-reported health condition data and health risk scores. All biometric and health data collected through these programs is classified as **sensitive personal information** under CPRA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ae)), triggering enhanced consent requirements and the right of consumers to limit its use and disclosure.

**Geolocation Data.** Vanterra\'s mobile application collects GPS coordinates, IP-derived location information, and wellness facility check-in location data. Precise geolocation data is classified as sensitive personal information under CPRA.

**Demographic and Identity Data.** Vanterra collects full names, dates of birth, email addresses, and other personal identifiers that, when combined with health and biometric data, create a comprehensive profile of each registered user.

**3.4 Data Broker Relationship Overview**

Vanterra maintains active commercial relationships with five third-party data brokers, with a combined total annual expenditure of \$3,645,000. These relationships are integral to Vanterra\'s marketing operations, audience targeting, and data enrichment strategies. Notably, Vanterra both **purchases** data from brokers and **shares** user-level personal information with brokers for enrichment and matching purposes --- that is, the data flows across these relationships are bidirectional in most cases.

The following table summarizes the five data broker relationships:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Broker**                      **Location**   **Contract Date**   **Annual Value**   **Primary Data Type**                         **Data Flow Direction**
  ------------------------------- -------------- ------------------- ------------------ --------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------
  DataLume Analytics, LLC         Austin, TX     Jan. 15, 2023       \$1,200,000        Audience segmentation, behavioral targeting   Bidirectional

  Prismara Insights Corp.         New York, NY   Mar. 1, 2022        \$680,000          Geolocation, foot-traffic analytics           Bidirectional

  NexTier Data Solutions, Inc.    Denver, CO     Sep. 10, 2023       \$440,000          Demographic/psychographic data                Inbound to Vanterra

  ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC      Chicago, IL    Jun. 1, 2022        \$950,000          Cross-device identity, behavioral data        Bidirectional (mutual exchange)

  Meridian Consumer Group, Inc.   Atlanta, GA    Nov. 20, 2023       \$375,000          Purchase history, loyalty data                Bidirectional
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All five data broker contracts were executed before the CPPA\'s final CPRA implementing regulations became effective on March 29, 2024. This is a significant factor in understanding the contractual compliance gaps identified in this audit: none of the agreements were drafted or negotiated with the CPPA\'s final regulatory requirements in mind.

Three of the five contracts --- DataLume, NexTier, and Meridian --- include generic \"CCPA compliance\" clauses that reference the original California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 and its initial implementing regulations. These clauses were drafted under the pre-CPRA legal framework and do not address CPRA-specific requirements such as the right to limit sensitive personal information, the distinction between \"sale\" and \"sharing,\" the enhanced opt-out requirements, or the specific contractual provisions mandated by the CPPA\'s final regulations for service provider and contractor relationships. The remaining two contracts --- Prismara and ClearPoint --- contain no specific California privacy compliance provisions whatsoever.

The contractual deficiencies across all five agreements are discussed in greater detail in Section 7.1 of this report.

**[4. Data Flow Diagrams]{.underline}**

**4.1 High-Level Data Flow Architecture**

The following narrative describes the high-level data flow architecture governing Vanterra\'s data exchanges with each of the five data brokers. This architecture was mapped by Pinehurst based on a review of technical documentation, data pipeline configurations, and interviews with Vanterra engineering personnel.

At the center of the architecture is Vanterra\'s user data platform, which aggregates personal information collected through the wellness platform\'s various intake channels (registration, biometric screenings, health risk assessments, app usage, and web browsing). From this central platform, data feeds are generated and transmitted to the data brokers according to the schedules and specifications described below.

**Vanterra → DataLume Analytics, LLC (Bidirectional):** Vanterra transmits the following data elements to DataLume on a weekly batch basis: user email addresses (plain text), full names (plain text), biometric-derived health segments (including BMI values, blood pressure readings, and cholesterol levels), browsing behavior data, and demographic data. The transfer method is **unsecured FTP** on port 21, without TLS/SSL encryption, using plain-text username and password authentication. DataLume processes this data and returns enriched audience segments and behavioral targeting profiles to Vanterra via the same FTP channel. DataLume uses the Vanterra data in combination with its own proprietary datasets and third-party data to create \"enhanced audience segments\" that DataLume markets and sells to its other commercial clients.

**Vanterra → Prismara Insights Corp. (Bidirectional):** Vanterra transmits user IDs, device identifiers, and geolocation data (GPS coordinates and wellness facility check-in locations) to Prismara on a daily batch basis via SFTP with AES-256 encryption and SSH key authentication. Prismara processes this data against its proprietary foot-traffic analytics platform and returns geolocation-derived wellness facility visit data, including frequency and duration of visits to fitness centers, health clinics, and pharmacies, matched to Vanterra user records.

**NexTier Data Solutions, Inc. → Vanterra (Inbound Only):** NexTier provides demographic and psychographic consumer data to Vanterra, including age range, income bracket, household composition, and lifestyle segment classifications. This data is delivered to Vanterra via a secure REST API (HTTPS with TLS 1.3, authenticated via API key and OAuth 2.0) on a monthly pull schedule. Vanterra does not transmit user-level personal information to NexTier. However, as noted in Section 5.3 below, NexTier\'s data is matched by Vanterra against its internal user database, which includes records of minor users.

**Vanterra → ClearPoint Behavioral, LLC (Bidirectional --- Mutual Exchange):** Vanterra transmits hashed email addresses, full names (plain text), and device identifiers to ClearPoint on a bi-weekly batch basis. The transfer method is **unsecured FTP** on port 21, without TLS/SSL encryption, using plain-text username and password authentication. The ClearPoint contract specifies that Vanterra will provide \"hashed email identifiers\" only; however, the actual data transfer files include both hashed and plain-text email addresses, as well as full names in plain text. This discrepancy between contractual specifications and operational practice is a significant finding discussed in Section 6.2. ClearPoint returns enriched behavioral profiles and cross-device graph mappings to Vanterra, enabling Vanterra to associate user activity across multiple devices.

**Vanterra → Meridian Consumer Group, Inc. (Bidirectional):** Vanterra transmits user IDs and health risk assessment response categories (categorized, not raw responses) to Meridian on a monthly batch basis via SFTP with AES-256 encryption and SSH key authentication. Meridian matches these records against its proprietary purchase history and loyalty program databases and returns matched consumer purchase behavior and loyalty data to Vanterra for integration into Vanterra\'s user profiles.

**Critical Security Observation:** Data flows to DataLume and ClearPoint involve the transmission of **unencrypted persistent identifiers** --- specifically, plain-text email addresses and full names --- via **unsecured FTP**. These transfers occur on regular automated schedules (weekly for DataLume, bi-weekly for ClearPoint) and affect the full California user dataset, including records of minor users. The absence of encryption on these channels creates a material risk of data interception and constitutes a failure to implement reasonable security procedures and practices as required by Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100(e).

**4.2 Sensitive Personal Information Data Flows**

Pinehurst conducted a specific assessment of data flows involving sensitive personal information as defined under CPRA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ae)). The following sensitive PI data flows were identified:

**Biometric Data to DataLume.** Biometric data collected through Vanterra\'s employer-sponsored wellness screenings --- specifically BMI, blood pressure readings, and cholesterol levels --- is transmitted to DataLume Analytics, LLC as part of the weekly data feed described in Section 4.1 above. DataLume uses this biometric data to create health-interest-based audience segments (e.g., \"high cholesterol concern,\" \"weight management active,\" \"cardiovascular risk\") that DataLume then sells to other commercial clients for targeted advertising purposes. This constitutes the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information for a purpose that goes significantly beyond what is necessary to provide the services reasonably expected by consumers who participate in an employer-sponsored wellness program.

**Health Questionnaire Data to Meridian.** Health risk assessment response categories derived from Vanterra\'s health questionnaires are transmitted to Meridian Consumer Group, Inc. and cross-referenced with Meridian\'s purchase history and loyalty program data at the individual user level. While the data transmitted to Meridian consists of categorized response summaries rather than raw questionnaire responses, health-related category classifications nevertheless constitute health information under CPRA and are subject to the enhanced protections afforded to sensitive personal information.

**Absence of Consent and Limitation Mechanisms.** No separate consent flow exists for the sharing of sensitive personal information with data brokers. Users who participate in biometric screenings consent to Vanterra\'s general privacy policy, which does not specifically address the sharing of biometric or health data with third-party data brokers for marketing or audience segmentation purposes. No \"Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information\" mechanism is available on Vanterra\'s website, mobile application, or within the user account settings. Consumers have no means of exercising their statutory right to limit the use and disclosure of their sensitive personal information.

**4.3 Minor User Data Flows**

Approximately 31,000 of Vanterra\'s 620,000 California-resident registered users are under the age of 16. These minor users access Vanterra\'s platform primarily through employer family wellness plans that extend coverage to employees\' minor dependents, including participation in school-based and family wellness screening programs.

Vanterra\'s platform does not implement any age-gating mechanism that would prevent minor user data from being included in outbound data broker transmissions. The data feed generation processes that produce the files transmitted to each data broker operate on the full California user dataset without applying age-based filters or flags. As a result, minor user records are included in the same data feeds as adult user records across all applicable data broker relationships.

The audit confirmed that minor user data is **not segregated** from adult user data in any of the five data broker data feeds. This means that all data elements transmitted to each broker --- including, for DataLume, plain-text email addresses, full names, and biometric data --- may include records of California users under the age of 16.

No affirmative opt-in consent mechanism exists for the sale or sharing of minors\' personal information. CPRA requires affirmative authorization from the consumer for users between the ages of 13 and 16, and from the consumer\'s parent or legal guardian for users under the age of 13. Vanterra has implemented neither mechanism. The platform\'s Terms of Service state a minimum age of 13 for account creation, but the audit identified accounts registered by users as young as 10 years of age through employer family wellness plan access pathways, and the Terms of Service do not require parental consent verification for account creation or data sharing.
